feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital communications roles: the progression at NACo is clear, the scope is substantial, and the content reads as polished and professional. It would be even stronger with tighter prioritization, more quantified outcomes beyond activity/scope, and a few wording/style fixes for consistency.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression and credibility: multiple promotions within one organization strongly signal trust, growth, and leadership.  
- Strong strategic/technical blend: combines digital strategy, CMS/platform work, analytics, governance, and multimedia in a way that fits senior communications roles well.  
- Generally polished writing with relevant detail: achievements like the 10,000+ page Drupal migration, studio buildout, and analytics stack expansion add impact.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more outcome metrics, not just scope: include results such as engagement growth, email performance, traffic gains, efficiency improvements, cost savings, or campaign impact.  
- Reduce duplication across “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT”; consolidate to improve structure and scannability.  
- Fix minor style/grammar consistency issues: “12 years experience” should be “12 years’ experience” or “12 years of experience”; keep serial comma usage consistent (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia” vs later lists without it); “A2/Learning” is slightly awkward—use “A2 (learning)” instead.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary with clear positioning, but it’s slightly generic and repeats themes covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tightening the language and adding a sharper value proposition will improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for cleaner, standard CV phrasing.
- Lead with your strongest differentiators: digital strategy, platform modernization, and mission-driven/public-sector communications.
- Trim channel lists slightly and emphasize outcomes or scope rather than broad capability stacking.
- Suggested rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience leading web, email, social, content, and multimedia programs for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in cross-channel strategy, platform modernization, and the workflows, governance, and systems that enable effective digital operations at scale. Strong background in advocacy communications, stakeholder alignment, and translating technical or policy issues into clear, accessible content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” and “workflows/systems” are repeated in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- “Advocacy messaging/stakeholder coordination” also appears elsewhere; keep the intro higher-level to avoid overlap.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. It would be sharper if it emphasized higher-value strategic strengths and used more consistent phrasing.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten and standardize terms: use parallel noun phrases and pluralize where needed (e.g., “Multi-channel communications,” “Web platform and CMS administration”).
- Prioritize differentiators tied to recent roles: digital transformation, CMS/platform modernization, analytics, governance, and advocacy communications.
- Reduce generic wording like “stakeholder & cross-department coordination” in favor of stronger, more senior language such as “Cross-functional leadership and stakeholder alignment.”
- Possible rewrite: Digital strategy and transformation • Web platform and CMS administration • Editorial workflows and content governance • Multi-channel communications • Data analytics and performance reporting • Workflow and systems architecture • Cross-functional leadership and stakeholder alignment • Policy and advocacy communications • Multimedia and live event production

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multi-channel communication,” “policy & advocacy communication,” and coordination themes repeat the header and Topline Skills.
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” also overlaps with Soft Skills; consider removing it here.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope, but it reads as a service list rather than a high-impact consulting entry. Tighten it around outcomes, senior advisory value, and only the work that is distinct from your prior NACo staff roles.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, Drupal platform enhancements, content operations, and AI-enabled discovery initiatives.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 3–4 impact-led bullets; e.g. combine systems/workflows/analytics/governance into one operations bullet.
- Rephrase for ownership and results: “Built modular Drupal microsite and toolkit frameworks for campaign storytelling” and “Led AI search initiative spanning retrieval design, structured content, and discovery UX.”
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/pages supported, campaign launches, toolkit downloads, publishing efficiency gains, search accuracy, or time-to-publish improvements.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Current wording overlaps heavily with the “Director of Digital Media” entry on governance, analytics, and enterprise web improvement.
- The microsite and AI search bullets also duplicate “Recent Projects”; keep this entry higher-level and reserve project specifics for that section.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact role with good scale metrics; it should read more like an executive achievement entry and less like a channel inventory. Emphasize transformation, team leadership, and business outcomes while trimming overlap with earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget, leading platform modernization and organization-wide communications operations.”
- Tighten and elevate bullets to outcomes: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Combine channel oversight into one concise bullet and add performance if available: email open/click rates, audience growth, engagement, production volume, or campaign results.
- Rephrase operational bullets to show impact: “Built NACo’s first in-house broadcast studio…” and “Implemented analytics stack across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery, improving executive reporting and decision-making.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Current email/social/video language overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry.
- “Governance/publishing workflows” also repeats themes from the consultant role; keep this version focused on enterprise-scale leadership.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry reads broad and overlaps with the more senior NACo roles. Tighten it around executional leadership, newsletter ownership, and the launch/expansion of repeatable video and editorial systems.

Suggested edit
- Open with scope + function: “Managed day-to-day digital communications operations across NACo’s web, email, social and video channels, supporting advocacy messaging and organization-wide editorial execution.”
- Make bullets more outcome-oriented: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Sharpen the video point: “Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one stronger systems statement: “Improved cross-team editorial planning and digital publishing workflows, increasing coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Led day-to-day digital communications operations” overlaps with the Director of Digital Media entry; use “managed” or “oversaw execution” here to preserve progression.
- Weekly video/livestream language also appears in the 2015–2018 role; frame this entry as scaling and formalizing the program, not starting it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this topline item is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header, core competencies, and recent NACo roles. It should sharpen toward senior, recent strengths and use more distinctive phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with tighter, higher-signal language focused on enterprise leadership:
- Enterprise digital strategy & web modernization
- Editorial governance, publishing workflows & content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership for public-sector organizations
- Audience-centered campaign, advocacy & storytelling strategy
- Consider changing “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” to “Public-sector communications strategy” to sound more senior and less tactical.
- Keep terms that align with recent roles: governance, analytics-informed operations, web modernization, and cross-channel leadership.
- If space allows, make one line outcome-oriented: “Led digital strategy and governance for a 10,000+ page Drupal platform serving 3.5M annual page views.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications” repeat the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Audience-focused content planning” is vague and partially duplicated by campaign/storytelling bullets in recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it reads as a generic tool dump and overlaps heavily with the Technical + IT section. For a topline skills area, emphasize higher-value platform leadership and modernization themes over listing every technology.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability-led phrasing, e.g. “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization” instead of separate platform names.
- Trim lower-priority or older-feeling items here; keep the most relevant to recent roles: Drupal, CMS modernization, API integrations, workflow automation, AI-enabled search.
- Group coding skills more tightly: “Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery)” rather than listing each as equal standalone skills.
- Suggested rewrite: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based content systems • AI-enabled search and discovery experiences”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- WordPress, SharePoint, and Power Pages are already covered in Technical + IT; consider removing them here unless central to target roles.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” overlaps with Core Competencies; consider “AI-enabled search and discovery” for variation.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it overlaps heavily with both “Core Competencies” and “Technical + IT.” Tighten it to emphasize decision-making and optimization, not just tool names.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe as a sharper mix of tools + outcomes: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity”
- Replace generic phrases with higher-value wording: “KPI framework development” instead of “KPI design”; “executive dashboarding and leadership reporting” instead of “Leadership reporting”
- Make optimization more specific: “SEO, UX and content performance analysis” instead of “SEO and performance analysis”
- Suggested version: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity • KPI framework development • Executive dashboarding and leadership reporting • SEO, UX and content performance analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT; consider making Topline Skills more strategic and leaving full tool lists to Technical + IT.
- “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” already appears in Core Competencies, so avoid repeating that exact framing.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and multiple NACo roles. Make it sharper by emphasizing higher-value, recent capabilities and using more specific phrasing.

Suggested edit
- Replace broad terms with more senior, delivery-focused language: “Broadcast-quality video production,” “livestream and hybrid event delivery,” “studio and control-room operations,” “PTZ camera direction,” “post-production editing.”
- Reorder by impact/recency: lead with livestream/hybrid events and studio operations, since these align with the in-house studio and event work in recent roles.
- Keep to 4–5 tightly grouped items; example:
- Broadcast-quality video production & post-production
- Livestream, hybrid & virtual event delivery
- Studio operations & control-room workflows
- PTZ camera systems & multi-camera production
- If space allows elsewhere, move tools like Premiere Pro/Audition to Technical + IT rather than listing them here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies; vary wording or remove one instance.
- “Video production” is supported in Work Experience, so avoid repeating generic phrasing without added specificity.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Since Drupal is central to recent roles, this item should emphasize depth/order rather than repeat broad skills.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, add light qualifiers to show level: **Drupal (enterprise/public-sector web modernization) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Consider renaming the heading to **CMS & Web Platforms** for cleaner phrasing.
- If you want more impact, replace the weakest item with a stronger platform distinction only if true, e.g., **Drupal 10** instead of generic Drupal.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates **Topline Skills → Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; keep the detailed platform list in one place and use the other for broader capabilities.
- “GitHub Pages” may feel lightweight versus the enterprise focus of the rest of the CV unless it supported a notable project.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This section should feel more implementation-focused and highlight modern, relevant tools over older ones.

Suggested edit
- Reframe around execution depth, e.g.: “Front-end implementation: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript • API and tag implementation: Google Tag Manager, API integrations • Edge/serverless tooling: Cloudflare Workers • Deployment automation: GitHub Actions”
- Consider dropping “jQuery” or moving it to the end as legacy support unless it is still central to current work.
- Use consistent category labels instead of a flat list to improve scanability and seniority.
- If space allows elsewhere, tie 1–2 tools to outcomes in recent roles (e.g., GTM for analytics deployment, Cloudflare Workers for performance or routing improvements).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- “GitHub Actions” may also overlap conceptually with “Workflow automation”; keep it here only if framed as CI/CD or deployment automation.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems leadership. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” and “Airtable systems” elsewhere, so it should be tighter and more differentiated.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Tools
- Reorder by strongest/relevant systems first: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Slack • Microsoft Teams • Trello • Basecamp
- Consider grouping for clarity: Automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Project/workflow: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | Collaboration: Slack, Microsoft Teams
- If space allows, add a light qualifier to show application, e.g. “Used to build editorial workflows, cross-team planning systems and lightweight automations.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills/Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same phrasing here.
- Slack/Teams are collaboration tools, not workflow systems; either regroup or move them if you want stricter categorization.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too bare to add much value on its own. It should signal level of use and avoid repeating the email leadership already covered strongly in recent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp (enterprise email marketing, newsletter operations, audience engagement)**
- If accurate, add proficiency/context rather than just tool names: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp • email campaign deployment • segmentation • journey automation**
- Keep the emphasis on current/recent platforms first; if Dynamics 365 is most current, leave it first and consider dropping Mailchimp if exposure was limited or older.
- Use consistent naming: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys** is cleaner and more current than “Customer Insights / Journeys.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with work-experience bullets about leading email/newsletter operations; don’t restate outcomes here unless you remove them elsewhere.
- “Engagement” is vague; avoid broadening into social/community tools unless those platforms are listed separately.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and specific to “firsts” or foundational contributions from this earlier period.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and foundation-building: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team and formalize workflows across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add clearer ownership: “Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and helped expand the organization’s in-house digital content capacity.”
- Tighten the management phrasing: replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with “mentored a digital media associate” or “supervised day-to-day work of a digital media associate.”
- If possible, add 1–2 metrics: number of livestreams/videos produced, audience growth, publishing volume, or efficiency gains from workflow improvements.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; frame this item as launching or establishing the format.
- “Strengthening workflows across web, email, social” is repeated elsewhere; keep this version focused on early team-building and production.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid foundation, but it reads generic and underplays the most distinctive achievement. For an older role, keep it brief and emphasize the podcast launch plus any concrete program/research support outcomes.

Suggested edit
- Lead with the standout result: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, guest coordination, and production.”
- Tighten the rest into one impact-oriented clause: “Coordinated innovation and research projects that supported county-focused programs and policy initiatives.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production” with specifics if available: multimedia briefs, web content, interviews, or promotional assets.
- If possible, add one metric or scope point: number of episodes, projects supported, stakeholders served, or departments/programs supported.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid repeating broad “digital content production and multimedia” language already covered more strongly in later NACo roles.
- Don’t overemphasize video/editorial operations here; later positions already establish that progression clearly.
